clue.text: Charles I wandering round an old English county

indicators.note: wandering round suggests the letters roaming about into a new order

explanation.surface: King Charles I tours the shires of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering round' signals an anagram of CHARLES I plus AN. Lancashire is a county in north-west England; the setter calls it old in the sense of long-established.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a historic shire of north-west England, one of the traditional counties.

clue.text: Confined in mental asylum, sad to say

indicators.note: confined in tells us the letters are shut up inside the words mental asylum

explanation.surface: Someone is sadly committed to a psychiatric hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of regret, used where one might say 'unfortunately' or 'sad to say'.

clue.text: Dress circle for the clergyman

indicators.note: dress here is a verb, to arrange or set in order, so the word circle is rearranged

explanation.surface: Theatre seating in the dress circle reserved for the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress circle' reads as the theatre's first balcony, but 'Dress' is the anagram signal working on CIRCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, a priest or minister.

clue.text: His initial confusion was amusing

parts.note: describes an Oxford don famous for comically swapping the first sounds of words, a mix-up of initials

explanation.surface: A man whose early muddles made people laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: William Archibald Spooner, Warden of New College, Oxford, gave his name to spoonerisms, where initial sounds are swapped ('a well-boiled icicle' for 'a well-oiled bicycle').
explanation.definitionFit: The Reverend Spooner is remembered for transposing the opening letters of words, to comic effect.

clue.text: Russian Ruler, one who takes the lead

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the van is the leading part of an army or procession, as in 'in the vanguard'

explanation.surface: A tsar described as a natural leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Several tsars bore the name, most famously Ivan the Terrible, ruler of Russia.

clue.text: Competitor in an event ran terribly

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the run of words event ran terribly

explanation.surface: A runner in a race who performed badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran terribly' looks like an anagram, but the letters sit unchanged across 'evENT RAN Terribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has entered a contest is a competitor in it.

clue.text: Chart showing relative positions

parts.note: relative is read as a noun, a relation, so the chart plots where each relation stands in a lineage

explanation.surface: A diagram showing where things stand compared with one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A genealogical diagram showing ancestors and descendants and how each relation is connected.

clue.text: Having started the race is wide of target

explanation.surface: A runner who has got going but is heading the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both having left the starting line and being inaccurate, missing the mark.

clue.text: Some leg of beef

parts.note: part of a leg, and also the young animal of beef cattle

explanation.surface: A cut of meat from the butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy back of the lower leg, and also a young bovine, the source of veal.

clue.text: Robust shoes will be

explanation.surface: Sturdy footwear is built for a long life.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the foot-shaped form a cobbler builds a shoe on, so shoes are literally made on a last.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means durable, built to endure; and footwear is shaped on a cobbler's last.

clue.text: Is among those left to fight

indicators.note: among tells us one piece goes in the middle of another

parts.note: the rest are those remaining or left over
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stays behind with the others to carry on the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to oppose or struggle against something.

clue.text: Washed up when everyone was in bed

indicators.note: was in places the second piece inside the first, between its letters

parts.note: taken as written
each, as in 'each and every one', stands for everyone

explanation.surface: Something came ashore during the night while the household slept.
explanation.definitionFit: A whale or boat washed up on the shore has been stranded there.

clue.text: Trippers may go to see something cheekily displayed by ladies

explanation.surface: Day-trippers and fashionable women each have their own attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: A trippers' scenic attraction, and a mole or patch worn on the cheek; 'cheekily' puns on where it sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenic place tourists visit, and a small dark mark on the face, often on the cheek.

clue.text: No jiggery pokery is beyond the grasp of directors

parts.note: something beyond one's grasp is above one, out of reach
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Honest dealing is something directors cannot manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Open and honest, with no trickery or underhand dealing.

clue.text: Attractive girl easily caught in the field

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman is easily won over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a dolly is a very easy catch for a fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a pretty young woman, and the cricket term for a simple catch offered to a fielder.

clue.text: Break down in the course of an investigation

definitions.text: Break down in the course of an investigation

parts.words: Break down in the course of an investigation
parts.note: break down here means examine piece by piece, as an investigator does, not collapse

explanation.surface: A detective cracks under the strain of a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something in detail by separating it into its parts, as an inquiry does.

clue.text: Request we turn to one side

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the word we in the other direction

explanation.surface: Asking a group to swing sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked, tilted away from straight.

clue.text: Rod, pole or perch

parts.note: rod, pole and perch are all old names for one unit of length, but perch is meant as a bird's resting place

explanation.surface: A list of old measures, each five and a half yards.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod, pole and perch are three names for the same old length, so the list looks like measurement; only 'perch' leads to a bird's resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch or place where birds settle to rest.

clue.text: A cat scrap

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Two cats fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight, but here it means a tiny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny particle or fragment, the smallest bit of something.

clue.text: This space sounds better ventilated

indicators.note: sounds tells us to say a word out loud and enter a word that sounds like it

parts.note: airier means having more fresh air, better ventilated

explanation.surface: A room that seems to have improved airflow.
explanation.definitionFit: A region or extent of space.

clue.text: Strips, being about to get some rest

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to peel is to strip off a covering

explanation.surface: Someone undresses before going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumber is a natural period of rest.

clue.text: Drinks up with a companion and leaves

indicators.note: in a down clue up shows the word is written bottom to top, reversing it

parts.note: nips are small drinks of spirits
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: Having a drink with a friend before going home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NIPS into SPIN. 'leaves' looks like a verb (departs) but is the plural noun for foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable, eaten for its foliage.

clue.text: Here's what you get for Christmas

explanation.surface: Handing over a festive gift.
explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is in attendance ('present and correct'); the other is a gift.

clue.text: Cure those people without charge

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: they means those people
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'take the rap'

explanation.surface: Treatment for them is free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without charge' reads as free of cost, but 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal, a remedy.

clue.text: Knew cry may come from a woodpecker

indicators.note: may come from suggests the letters of knew cry are reworked to produce something new

explanation.surface: A bird's call is recognised.
explanation.definitionFit: The wryneck is a small bird of the woodpecker family, named for twisting its neck.

clue.text: Not one on view

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nothing is visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on view' looks like a phrase, but 'view' alone is the definition, meaning an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea or opinion, a belief someone holds.

clue.text: Work hard with an advertising jingle

parts.note: to slog is to toil or work hard

explanation.surface: Putting effort into composing a catchy commercial tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy phrase used in advertising, like a jingle's tagline.

clue.text: A delay upsets this celebration

indicators.note: in a down clue upsets turns the pieces upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: a lag is a delay, as in time lag

explanation.surface: A party postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' looks like an anagram signal, but it turns A LAG backwards to read GAL A.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive occasion or special entertainment.

clue.text: It develops in the East and breaks round the West

definitions.text: It develops in the East and breaks round the West

parts.words: It develops in the East and breaks round the West
parts.note: describes daybreak, which begins in the east and spreads round to the west

explanation.surface: Something growing in Asia and spreading to Europe and America.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a movement or idea spreading from East to West; it is daybreak, which 'breaks' in the east first.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak, the first light of morning, which appears in the eastern sky.

clue.text: Bill gets medical qualification of college

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Bill gets medical qualification of college' (10): AC (bill) plus an anagram of MEDICAL gives one letter short of ACADEMICAL and no anagram indicator; no scan or online source gives the full clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Bill gets medical qualification of college

clue.text: I returned to receive the king-a terrible person

indicators.note: to receive means the reversed piece takes another inside it
returned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone comes back to greet the monarch, who is a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster in folk tales, used of a cruel or frightening person.

clue.text: Encouraging a number to take part in an audition

indicators.note: to take part in places the number inside the other piece

parts.note: a hearing is an audition, a trial performance
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A singer is invited to try out for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartening news gives cheer and lifts the spirits.
